title: pact-identity: the library boundary
description: Every function a port of pact-identity presents, as `call(name, args) -> answer`: what it takes, what it answers, and which error codes it can fail with. This file is the source; CONTRACT.md is rendered from it and js/parity.mjs holds both ports to it.

why.description: One line, in this library's own words — never another library's error text, which a second port could not reproduce.

ErrorCode.description: Why a call failed. `bad_request`: an argument is missing or unusable as asked. `parse`: bytes that are there and will not read. `unsupported`: an algorithm or a function this library does not have. `envelope_invalid`: SPEC §12's code, for an envelope that does not open or prove itself. `vault`: the vault refused. `key` and `internal` are declared so a caller's switch has a name for them; no input known reaches either.

B64url.description: Bytes, as base64url without padding. An ANSWER always spells them this way. An ARGUMENT is read forgivingly about padding and alphabet (§0); the members of an envelope that travelled are not (§5).

Instant.description: An RFC 3339 UTC instant with second precision, as every answer writes one.

InstantIn.description: An RFC 3339 UTC instant as an argument: a fraction of a second is allowed and DROPPED, because the boundary is whole seconds.

Tbs.description: A TBSCertificate, DER: the bytes an external signer signs.

SigAlg.description: An AlgorithmIdentifier, DER — the TBS's own third field.

Serial.description: A certificate serial number, 8 to 20 bytes. Absent, the core draws 8 random bytes.

Form.description: How the sender proves itself inside the plaintext: its whole chain, or the fingerprint of a leaf the recipient already holds.

Envelope.description: A sealed envelope as this library WRITES one (SPEC §13.1).

ArrivedEnvelope.description: An envelope as it ARRIVED: four strings, which may be anything. Judging their spelling is the function's work, not the caller's.

key_usage.description: The bit positions that are set.

extensions.description: Every extension in the order the certificate carries them.

Certificate.description: A certificate read back. `profile_error` judges it as a root when it is self-issued and a CA, otherwise as a leaf.

leaf_fingerprint.description: Which leaf this pin holds (§5). Optional: with it, only the pin that matched is parsed.

Pin.description: A contact as the host holds it. `state` absent is `active`.

NodeState.description: What the host knows, handed to `decide` whole. Every list absent is empty; `accept_new_hosts` absent is `auto`.

Decision.description: What `decide` decided. `code` says which shape this is.

Effect.description: Something the host must apply. `decide` changes nothing itself.

Kdf.description: The key derivation, as a vault DOCUMENT carries it: all four members, each inside its range. The ranges are checked at both ends on both paths, by one parser — an unbounded reader hands an attacker's file a 256 GiB allocation, and an unbounded writer seals a person's root behind a KDF a laptop brute-forces. A value that does not fit in 32 bits is out of range, never truncated.

KdfArgs.description: The same, as an ARGUMENT to `vault_seal`: every member may be left out and takes the default (64 MiB, t 3, p 1), and what is given is held to the same range as a document's.

LedgerEntry.description: One leaf the wallet issued: the endpoint and the dates, which is what every rule reads. Never the leaf itself, which is the host's to serve and grants nothing (SPEC §9).

VaultRoot.description: One identity the wallet holds. In the file it carries the root's key (`pkcs8`) or names the card that does (`holder`); in the record it carries neither, until the root is re-bound (SPEC §9): then `rebound_at` (ms) marks the entry and `pkcs8` stays with it.

VaultPasskey.description: The credential a derived root belongs to (SPEC §2.1); not secret.

VaultContact.description: The wallet's own copy of one contact (SPEC §9): pinned by root, at an endpoint, under the person's name; a leaf and the root certificate when the wallet has seen them.

VaultPlaintext.description: What the FILE seals: the root and nothing else (SPEC §9). `prf` is the §2.1 secret a derived root's record is opened with, for the wallet that has lost its credential. A `v` that is not 2 is refused at both ends and nothing converts.

RecordPlaintext.description: What the RECORD seals (SPEC §9): the ledger and the contact book, the roots without their keys — or with one, once a root has been re-bound — and what the wallet page keeps beside them. Under the store key of §2.1 for a wallet with a credential; beside the file, under the recovery key, for one without.

version.notes: The build, not a rule: `spec` is the version of `pact-protocol/SPEC.md` the port implements and is the same everywhere; the other member names the port's own release, so the answers differ and nothing compares them.

key_from_seed.notes: An Ed25519 seed is used directly; a P-256 scalar is the seed mod n, with 0 → 1 (the seed library's `keys.mjs`). Written for the vectors, and production API since SPEC §2.1: it is how a wallet turns a derived seed into its root.

prf_salt.notes: SPEC §2.1's fixed PRF input, `SHA-256("pact/vault/1")`, and the three `info` strings. A call rather than a constant a caller copies, so the bytes live in one place and the vectors prove them.

derive_seed.notes: `HKDF-SHA256(ikm = prf, salt = "", info, L = 32)`. **Refuses an `info` outside the three, and a `prf` that is not 32 bytes.** Both refusals are the point rather than hygiene: a mistyped domain separator would otherwise return 32 perfectly good bytes and silently derive an identity belonging to nobody, which is the one failure the derived-root design exists to prevent.

key_info.notes: `key_id` is the 32 raw bytes of the fingerprint's hash.

sign.notes: Ed25519 pure, or ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 in ASN.1 DER, **always the low-S twin** (`s ≤ n/2`, SPEC §14.1): a library returns either twin of an ECDSA signature, and a port returns one.

root_tbs.notes: The external-signing seam: a root in a passkey or a security key signs `tbs` in the host, and `assemble_root` builds the certificate from the signature handed back.

assemble_root.notes: `sig_alg` is read from the TBS; when one is handed back it must be equal, so the algorithm outside a certificate can never differ from the one inside. **An ECDSA `sig` is normalised to its low-S twin** before assembling: what arrives at the seam was made by a token or a KMS that has never heard of §14.1, and swapping a signature for its twin needs no key. Anything that is not an ECDSA value passes through untouched.

build_leaf.notes: Refuses a validity over 398 days and an endpoint that is not an https URL in normal form.

leaf_tbs.notes: The same seam for leaves: `build_leaf` with the root's public key in place of its private one.

parse_certificate.notes: Parsing itself refuses, with a `parse` error, what DER has one encoding for and the certificate spells another way: the AlgorithmIdentifier inside the TBS differing from the one outside (`signature algorithm inside and outside differ`), a BOOLEAN that is not `0xFF` or is an explicit FALSE, a non-minimal INTEGER, an OBJECT IDENTIFIER with a padded subidentifier, a `keyUsage` BIT STRING whose unused bits are set or whose trailing zero bits are not removed, a validity of other than two times, an extension of other than two or three parts or whose OCTET STRING holds more than one TLV, a P-256 key that is not the uncompressed point. Every one of these is a scenario in `vectors/intrude.mjs`, which the seed and both ports answer alike — the seed's strictness and the ports' are one rule, proven rather than asserted.

kind.description: `root` or `leaf`. **Declared, not enforced**: both ports compare it with `"root"` and judge anything else as a leaf, so a third value is read as `leaf` rather than refused. Narrowing it is a change to the Rust core, which costs a re-pin, so it waits for a change that pays for one.

profile_error.notes: The exact strings of the seed's `x509.mjs profileError`; `null` when the certificate is inside the profile. This is an ANSWER whose one member happens to be called `error`: a failure of the call carries `why` beside it (§0), and this never does.

validate_chain.notes: SPEC §14.2's rules in order. A refusal is an answer, not a failure of the call: `rule` says which one refused.

address_guard.notes: Refuses a host that is a loopback, link-local, private, unspecified or CGNAT literal (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127/8`, `10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`, `169.254/16`, `100.64/10`, `0.0.0.0`, `::1`, `::`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`, deprecated site-local `fec0::/10`, NAT64's local-use `64:ff9b:1::/48`), an IPv6 literal that EMBEDS such an IPv4 address — IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible `::/96`, NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96`, 6to4 `2002::/16` — because a translator dials the address inside (`[64:ff9b::7f00:1]` is loopback on a NAT64 network, and a literal has no name to resolve, so this is the whole guard), and, for a guest, an endpoint equal to `self_endpoint`. DNS resolution is the host's; `ip_is_private` is exposed so the host applies the same predicate to what it resolves.

csr_check.notes: Refuses a bad signature (no proof of possession), a key equal to any root in `root_spkis` (the root-key refusal), an endpoint that is not normal https, an endpoint the address guard refuses. `root_spkis` absent is no roots; present and unreadable is an error, never "no roots to refuse against".

issue_from_csr.notes: `csr_check` first — with the issuing root added to `root_spkis` — then `build_leaf` under the monotonic rule. `valid_days` absent is 365; an explicit 0 is refused.

issue_tbs_from_csr.notes: As `issue_from_csr`, for the seam: assembled with `assemble_leaf`.

seal.description: `none`, `optional` or `required` (SPEC §3). **Declared, not enforced**: a non-empty value is written into `X-PACT-SEAL` as given, so a fourth word makes a card whose policy no reader implements. Narrowing it is a change to the Rust core, which costs a re-pin, so it waits for a change that pays for one. What IS refused is a control character, in this member and every other one a caller supplies.

extra.description: Whole lines, written after the certificate.

card_encode.notes: Folded per RFC 6350 at 75 octets, CRLF, exactly as the seed's `card.mjs`. Refuses `<fn|seal|extra> carries a control character`: a card is lines, and a line break in anything a caller supplies writes a property of the caller's choosing (SPEC §3).

ignored.description: Property names the card carried and this library does not read.

card_decode.notes: Every refusal is `bad_request` with the exact `why` strings of `card.mjs`.

hpke_seal.notes: `ephemeral_seed` exists for vectors and the intrusion suite; production callers omit it and the core draws 32 fresh bytes. `aad` absent is empty.

seal_request.notes: `form` absent is `chain`, which needs `sender_chain`; `method` absent is `tools/call`; `params` absent is `{}`; `exp` absent is `ts + 600`; `cty` absent is a call.

open_result.notes: The caller side of §13.2: opens, requires `result` xor `error` plus one of `chain`/`leaf`, validates the chain to `expected_root` and `expected_endpoint` or finds the named leaf among `pins`, refuses a superseded leaf, verifies `sig`, checks `cty` and `msg_id`. Every refusal of the ENVELOPE is `{"error": "envelope_invalid", "why"}`. `leaf_update` is a leaf newer than the pin, for the host to store.

follow_renewed.notes: §14.4: `answer` is the peer's `{"code": "certificate_renewed", "data": {"chain"}}`, whatever it actually sent. Validate to the pinned root and the dialed address, and follow only when the chain is newer than or equal to the pin.

vault_seal.notes: `plaintext` is a VaultPlaintext or a RecordPlaintext, and its `v` is 2: anything else is `bad_request` (`a vault plaintext is v 2: the root, or the record`). That generation is all `vault_seal` checks of the plaintext (and `vault_open` of what it opens): the two shapes are held by `wallet_issue`, where the rules read them, so a stricter seal or open cannot lock a person out of a document a wallet already keeps. Read in this order: `passphrase` (absent: `passphrase is required`; empty: `empty passphrase`), `plaintext` and its generation, then `kdf`. `salt` and `nonce` are for tests only.

vault_open.notes: A wrong passphrase and a tampered document are one message. A document that opens to a plaintext whose `v` is not 2 was written by an earlier wallet and is refused (`vault`, `this vault was written by an earlier wallet and is not opened: there is no conversion`); nothing converts.

wallet_issue.notes: Two documents, as §9 keeps them: the vault is the root and nothing else, the record holds the ledger this reads and the entry answered is appended to. A vault carrying `ledger` or `contacts` is refused (`bad_request`, `a vault holds the root and nothing else: its ledger and contacts belong in the record`); a missing record is refused (`record_plaintext is required: the ledger lives there`). After `root_fingerprint`, `csr`, `now` and `valid_days` (present and not an integer: `valid_days is required`), each document is held to its schema before anything in it is read: the vault (not an object: `vault_plaintext is required: the root lives there`; then its `v`; then the first member, in sorted order, it does not hold: `vault_plaintext holds v, roots, prf and passkey, and nothing else: <member>`), then the record (likewise, `record_plaintext holds v, roots, ledger, contacts, passkey and backup_verified_at, and nothing else: <member>`; a `ledger` that is not a list: `the record's ledger is a list`), and every ledger entry, every root's: an entry that is not an object, lacks a required member, has one of the wrong type or an instant that does not parse, or carries one it does not hold is refused (`the record's ledger entry <i> does not read: <member>`), never skipped — skipped, it could be the live leaf. A root with no `pkcs8` is refused (`this root is held on a card: wallet_issue signs only with a key the vault holds`). The entry answered is the endpoint and the dates, never the leaf. The wallet's rules: `csr_check` with the vault's roots as `root_spkis`; `new_host` true when no ledger entry names that endpoint's host, with the warning `new host: this endpoint's host has never been issued to`; the **live leaf is the newest one issued** (§14.3) and a second endpoint while it is unexpired is refused unless `move: true`, which instead warns `move: the live leaf at the previous endpoint is superseded once contacts see this one`; `not_before` monotonic over the ledger; `valid_days` absent means 365 and an explicit 0 is refused.
